#### 1. [prompts.chat](https://github.com/f/prompts.chat) (`f/prompts.chat`)
- **Official URL**: [https://github.com/f/prompts.chat](https://github.com/f/prompts.chat)
- **Project Homepage**: [https://prompts.chat](https://prompts.chat)
- **Primary Language**: `HTML` | **Stars**: `★ 164,436` | **License**: `NOASSERTION`
- **Catalog Provenance**: Channel: *ig_scraper* | Video: *IG Scraper Links* | Published: *2026-09-23*
- **Attached Keywords**: `openai, ai, prompt-engineering, mcp, open-source, llm, claude`

**Product Description Text**:
> https://github.com/f/prompts

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> prompts.chat is the world's largest open-source prompt library for AI chat models, originally launched in December 2022 as "Awesome ChatGPT Prompts" and now compatible with ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Mistral, and other major assistants. It solves the problem of prompt discovery and sharing by providing a curated, community-driven collection that users can browse, contribute to, and export in multiple formats including CSV and Markdown. Beyond the prompt library, the project includes educational resources such as a free 28+ chapter interactive book on prompt engineering covering chain-of-thought reasoning, few-shot learning, and AI agents, plus a game-based "Prompting for Kids" experience for ages 8-14. The platform offers flexible self-hosting capabilities with a setup wizard supporting custom branding, themes, and authentication via GitHub, Google, or Azure AD, built on a modern web stack with PostgreSQL (via Neon) and deployable through Docker. Developers can integrate the library directly into their workflows through a CLI tool, Claude Code plugin, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, making prompts accessible from within AI-powered development environments. With 143k+ GitHub stars, recognition as a GitHub Staff Pick, references from institutions like Harvard and Columbia, and endorsements from AI leaders at OpenAI, Hugging Face, and GitHub, it serves prompt engineers, AI researchers, educators, and developers seeking to enhance their AI interactions.

**Product Description Text**:
> User-friendly WebUI for LLMs (Formerly Ollama WebUI)

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Open WebUI is a self-hosted, offline-capable AI platform that provides a user-friendly interface for interacting with large language models, addressing the need for a private, extensible alternative to cloud-based AI chat services. It supports multiple LLM runners including Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible API (such as LMStudio, GroqCloud, and vLLM), enabling users to mix local and remote inference providers seamlessly. Key features include built-in Retrieval Augmented Generation with support for nine vector databases, granular role-based access control, a robust plugin system with MCP integration, and collaborative tools like shared Channels, persistent memory, and AI-assisted scheduling. It offers a responsive Progressive Web App with full Markdown/LaTeX rendering, voice and video calling capabilities, image generation, multi-model conversations, and enterprise-ready features such as LDAP/SSO/SCIM authentication, OpenTelemetry observability, and horizontal scalability via Redis. Ideal for developers, IT administrators, research teams, and enterprises seeking a customizable, secure AI deployment, Open WebUI is built with a modern technology stack including Python (backend), Svelte/TypeScript (frontend), Docker/Kubernetes support, and flexible database options (SQLite or PostgreSQL).

**Product Description Text**:
> The open source Firebase alternative. Supabase gives you a dedicated Postgres database to build your web, mobile, and AI applications.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Supabase is an open-source Postgres development platform that provides a Firebase-like developer experience for building web, mobile, and AI applications. It combines enterprise-grade tools—including a hosted PostgreSQL database, PostgREST for auto-generated REST and GraphQL APIs, GoTrue for JWT-based authentication, realtime websocket subscriptions, S3-compatible file storage, edge functions, and a vector/embeddings toolkit for AI workloads. Developers can use it as a managed cloud service or self-host it locally, with modular client libraries available for JavaScript, Flutter, Swift, and other languages. The platform is aimed at developers seeking a scalable, relational backend without vendor lock-in, leveraging Postgres as its foundation. Community support is provided through GitHub Discussions, Discord, and dedicated issue tracking, while an intuitive dashboard simplifies database management and configuration.

**Product Description Text**:
> The open and composable observability and data visualization platform. Visualize metrics, logs, and traces from multiple sources like Prometheus, Loki, Elasticsearch, InfluxDB, Postgres and many more.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Grafana is an open-source observability and data visualization platform that helps users query, explore, and understand metrics, logs, and traces from multiple data sources such as Prometheus, Loki, Elasticsearch, InfluxDB, and Postgres. It solves the challenge of monitoring distributed systems by providing a unified interface for creating dynamic, reusable dashboards with template variables and flexible client-side visualizations through panel plugins. DevOps engineers, SREs, and platform teams rely on Grafana for ad-hoc data exploration, drilldowns, and side-by-side comparisons of time ranges and queries, as well as for visually defining alert rules that integrate with notification systems like Slack, PagerDuty, and OpsGenie. The platform supports mixing multiple data sources within a single graph, enabling per-query data source selection and compatibility with custom datasources. Distributed under the AGPL-3.0 license, Grafana is built with a modern web technology stack and is actively developed with extensive documentation, contributing guidelines, and a vibrant community on Slack and discussion forums.

> Stop renting your intelligence. Own it with AnythingLLM. Everything you need for a powerful local-first agent experience

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> AnythingLLM is an all-in-one, local-first AI application that enables users to build a private, fully-featured ChatGPT-style assistant capable of chatting with documents, automating workflows, and deploying AI agents without cloud dependency. It solves the problem of vendor lock-in and data privacy concerns by allowing users to connect any local or cloud LLM—including OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, LM Studio, and dozens more—while keeping documents, embeddings, and conversations on their own infrastructure. Key features include a no-code AI agent builder, MCP compatibility, dynamic model routing, automatic and user-managed memories, scheduled tasks, intelligent skill selection that reduces token usage by up to 80%, multi-user permissioning, and support for multiple vector databases (LanceDB, PGVector, etc.) and document types. It is designed for developers, privacy-conscious professionals, and teams who want production-ready RAG and agent capabilities out of the box without complex setup. Available as a desktop application (Mac, Windows, Linux) and a Docker-deployable server, it includes a full developer API for custom integrations and an embeddable chat widget for websites.

**Product Description Text**:
> 🔥 🔥 🔥 Open Source Airtable Alternative

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> NocoDB is an open-source, self-hostable alternative to Airtable that lets users build and manage databases through a friendly spreadsheet-like interface, eliminating the need for SQL expertise. It transforms any existing SQL database into a no-code platform, enabling teams to create, read, update, and delete tables, columns, and rows with operations like sorting, filtering, grouping, and hiding columns. The platform supports multiple view types including Grid, Gallery, Form, Kanban, and Calendar, along with features like collaborative views, access controls, and automations. It's designed for product managers, operations teams, and developers who want database flexibility without vendor lock-in, offering full data ownership through self-hosting. NocoDB is easy to deploy via Docker, with support for SQLite or PostgreSQL backends, and includes a one-command "Auto-upstall" option that provisions the full stack (PostgreSQL, Redis, Traefik, SSL) for production use. Pre-built binaries are also available for macOS, Linux, and Windows for quick local testing.

Built by Garry Tan as the production memory behind his OpenClaw and Hermes deployments, it manages 155,795 pages across 24,589 people and 5,340 companies with 66 autonomous cron jobs running 24/7 for ingestion, enrichment, and overnight memory consolidation.

The system combines two core capabilities: a synthesis layer that produces well-cited prose responses (rather than returning search chunks) plus explicit gap analysis noting what the brain doesn't yet know, and a self-wiring knowledge graph that extracts typed entity relationships like `works_at`, `invested_in`, and `attended` on every page write without LLM calls. GBrain targets individual developers wanting a personal knowledge agent, YC-style teams needing scoped shared institutional memory (each user gets a permissioned slice with zero cross-leak fuzz-tested across all read paths), and AI agent builders wiring it in as a supercharged retrieval layer for Claude Code or Codex. The stack runs on PostgreSQL via PGLite (database ready in 2 seconds, no server required), Bun, and integrates through MCP, with install paths supporting everything from a 15-minute Codex setup to a full 30-minute always-on daemon deployment.

Workflows are agent-driven via a CLI (`pip install wrenai`) and a lightweight discovery stub installable into Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, and Codex, letting existing agents orchestrate setup, querying, and dashboard deployment. Generated answers can be turned into shareable, browser-side dashboards using the included `wren-core-wasm` SDK, deployable to Vercel or Cloudflare Pages with a single command. WrenAI is licensed under Apache 2.0 and is aimed at agent builders and data teams who need governed, Git-friendly BI outputs without maintaining yet another closed-source tool.

**Product Description Text**:
> ⚠️ Browser fingerprinting via favicon!

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Supercookie demonstrates a browser fingerprinting technique that exploits the favicon cache (F-Cache) to assign persistent, unique identifiers to website visitors. By serving favicons from a combinatorial set of URL paths and observing which requests are made versus served from cache, a server can reconstruct a binary pattern that identifies a browser with 100% accuracy. Unlike conventional cookies, this tracking method survives cache flushing, browser restarts, VPN usage, incognito/private mode, and even certain anti-tracking service workers, making it a significant privacy concern. The repository includes a fully functional web server (deployable via Docker or Node.js) that performs the favicon-based tracking, along with a live demo and comprehensive documentation explaining the threat model. Inspired by academic research from the University of Illinois, Chicago, it serves as an educational tool to raise awareness of this stealth tracking vector affecting all major desktop and mobile browsers. The technology stack is lightweight, relying on a Node.js backend with a configurable environment for hosting the tracking infrastructure.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> pgmicro is an in-process reimplementation of PostgreSQL, built in Rust and backed by a SQLite-compatible storage engine. It is an experimental fork of the Turso project, designed to create a fast, embeddable, single-file database. Unlike other approaches, pgmicro does not translate PostgreSQL syntax to SQLite; instead, it parses the PostgreSQL language directly and compiles it into SQLite bytecode. This process leverages PostgreSQL's powerful query capabilities while utilizing SQLite's simplicity for ephemeral environments. pgmicro is specifically designed to serve as a scratch database for AI agents and other low-touch applications. It achieves this by using a faithful PostgreSQL parser to generate SQLite-compatible instructions.

**Product Description Text**:
> better-drizzle is a lightweight repository layer that wraps an existing Drizzle ORM client to eliminate repetitive query boilerplate while preserving Drizzle's SQL-first type safety. It exposes a consistent, table-scoped API (`findMany`, `findFirst`, `create`, `update`, `delete`, `paginate`, `cursor`, `count`, `exists`, `upsert`, `upsertMany`, etc.) with typed nested relation filters, batched `include`/`select`, correlated `_count` subqueries, and atomic `connect`/`disconnect`/`set` relation writes. Transactions, row-level locking (PostgreSQL/MySQL), and a thenable `.explain()` for query plans are handled at the client level, and dynamic `client.repository(name)` resolution lets callers grab delegates by schema key or table name. - **Attached Keywords**: `postgresql, python, workflow, orchestration`
- **GitHub Topics**: `dbos, durable, temporal, workflow`

**Product Description Text**:
> DBOSify is a drop-in replacement for Temporal Python that uses Postgres—via the DBOS Transact library—as its workflow orchestration backend, eliminating the need for a separate Temporal server. It enables developers to run durable workflows, activities, signals, updates, retries, and recovery using only a Postgres database as infrastructure. At its core, a deterministic interpreter executes each workflow coroutine and its signal, update, and query handlers on a virtual event loop that advances only when events arrive, checkpointing all nondeterministic actions in Postgres before the workflow observes them. Activities and timers become DBOS steps and durable sleeps; signals, updates, and cancellations are delivered through Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY; and namespaces map to distinct Postgres schemas. The library is aimed at Python developers building reliable, long-running applications who want Temporal's durable execution semantics without the operational overhead of running a Temporal cluster. It is tested through ported Temporal unit and integration tests, sample applications, kill-and-recover scenarios, and signature-parity checks, though it is not wire-compatible with other Temporal SDKs and lacks the Temporal Web UI or CLI tooling.

**Product Description Text**:
> pgContext is a PostgreSQL 17 and 18 extension that transforms Postgres into a full AI search engine, combining dense vector search, metadata-filtered approximate search, and hybrid (dense + full-text) retrieval within the existing database. It solves the typical pain point of retrieval stacks that require a separate vector service, duplicated data, and additional backup, replication, and authorization boundaries by keeping retrieval alongside the source data. The extension supports HNSW indexes stored as durable PostgreSQL index pages, multiple distance metrics (L2, inner-product, cosine, L1), filter-aware ANN with Qdrant-style `must`/`should`/`must_not` predicates over registered columns and JSONB paths, and exact re-scoring of every candidate under MVCC, ACL, and RLS visibility. Benchmarks on the GloVe-100-angular dataset show pgContext matching pgvector's recall while answering queries 3.8–5.3× faster, or reaching 0.91 recall@10 at ~2.5 ms where pgvector reaches 0.75. It is built by Evokoa, distributed under Apache-2.0, and targeted at teams that want production-grade semantic and hybrid search without bolting on a second system.

**Product Description Text**:
> Syncular is an offline-first data synchronization framework that keeps an SQLite database on each client and reconciles changes through a server-owned commit log, enabling apps to read locally and continue working without connectivity. Writes update local state immediately, enter an outbox, and are validated by the server during sync, with a formally specified wire protocol verified by shared byte-level conformance tests across both TypeScript and Rust cores. The browser client uses SQLite on OPFS, while native platforms—Rust, Swift, Kotlin, Flutter, React Native, and Tauri—share the Rust core and native SQLite bindings. Servers run on Bun, Node, or Cloudflare Workers and support SQLite, Postgres, or D1 storage backends. Optional packages provide Yjs CRDT integration, column-level encryption, schema/query code generation for multiple languages, React hooks, and an in-process testkit for deterministic fault-injection testing. It targets developers building offline-capable, multi-platform applications who need reliable local-first storage with conflict-free replication without giving up SQL.

- **Catalog Provenance**: Channel: *Github Awesome* | Video: *Hacker News Show #10: mindwalk, spaceprojectsim, dom-docx, ctx, codealmanac, bramble, remux, leaves* | Published: *2026-07-26*
- **Attached Keywords**: `sqlite, database, postgresql, nodejs, typescript`
- **GitHub Topics**: `bun, codegen, javascript, postgresql, sql, sqlite`

**Product Description Text**:
> bun-sqlgen is a code generation tool that brings type safety to raw SQL queries in Bun applications without requiring an ORM. It solves the problem of untyped database results by analyzing SQL statements against a known schema and producing accurate TypeScript types for each query's return shape. The tool treats migrations as the single source of truth for the database schema, parsing them through an in-memory PGlite (Wasm Postgres) engine so no live database connection is needed during code generation. Developers wrap their `Bun.sql` client with a `withTypes` helper and tag queries with unique names, after which the generator emits a `.gen.d.ts` file declaring precise result types—catching column-name typos and null-safety violations at compile time with standard `tsc`. It is built on Bun's runtime and uses PGlite for schema introspection, making it ideal for Bun developers who want the performance and control of raw SQL without sacrificing TypeScript's type guarantees. Runnable examples in the repository demonstrate end-to-end usage with realistic schemas and queries.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> pgsemantic by varmabudharaju is a zero-config semantic search tool for any PostgreSQL database. Installation is just 'pip install pgsemantic' followed by three commands to enable vector-style semantic search against existing tables without requiring schema migrations, additional extensions, or external services beyond an embedding provider (typically OpenAI or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint). The library auto-detects text columns, generates embeddings, stores them in lightweight side tables or HNSW/ivfflat indexes depending on configuration, and exposes a simple SQL function (or thin ORM helper) for similarity queries — typically SELECT ... ORDER BY pgsemantic.match(...) LIMIT k. Use cases include building RAG pipelines on top of existing Postgres data, adding semantic filters to traditional CRUD apps, and prototyping search features without standing up a separate vector database. License: MIT (per the public repository). This synopsis is based on the in-source description ('Zero-config semantic search for any PostgreSQL database. pip install pgsemantic, three commands, don...'), the project name, and standard patterns for semantic-search libraries targeting Postgres.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> SketchLog is a streaming metrics compression engine that condenses high-throughput telemetry streams—up to 100M events—into bounded-memory, mergeable statistical summaries as small as 93 KB. It solves the storage and query cost problem of retaining raw event data by combining DDSketch for latency percentiles, HyperLogLog for cardinality estimation, and Count-Min Sketch for event frequencies within a single StreamLog container. The framework ships with a FastAPI server, Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs, streaming SQL analytics, Smart SLO workflows, multi-tenancy with namespace quotas, and an Authenticated Sketch Mesh for distributed sketch aggregation across nodes. Production deployments are supported through Docker images, Helm charts, Kubernetes Operator manifests, and flexible durability options including PostgreSQL/SQLAlchemy or the optional OmniKV embedded backend. SRE teams, platform engineers, and observability practitioners running services at scale would use it to retain operational signal—p99 latencies, unique user counts, event frequencies—without the cost of full-fidelity telemetry storage, complementing existing stacks like Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, and Datadog.

Asynchronous communication flows through RabbitMQ on top of Wolverine, leveraging durable inbox and outbox patterns for reliable event delivery, while synchronous service-to-service calls use gRPC and cross-cutting traffic is routed through a YARP API gateway. PostgreSQL stores write models, MongoDB serves read models, and all auth is centralized in Duende IdentityServer, with full observability through OpenTelemetry, Jaeger, Prometheus, and Grafana. Comprehensive tests cover unit, integration, end-to-end, and contract scenarios using xUnit, Testcontainers, and PactNet. The solution targets backend architects and .NET developers learning production-grade microservices patterns, and can be run locally with .NET Aspire, Docker Compose, or deployed to Kubernetes with cert-manager and Nginx Ingress.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> **effect-mq** — Effect-native background job processing for TypeScript

A schema-first job queue built on [Effect](https://effect.website) v4 that brings the proven semantics of BullMQ — retries, repeatable schedules, deduplication, and worker runtimes — into Effect's typed, structured-concurrency world. Jobs are defined as class schemas with payloads, success types, idempotency keys, and retry defaults baked in, eliminating string-based handler lookup and untyped payloads.

The package splits into tree-shakeable modules: `effect-mq` for the storage-agnostic core, `drizzle-postgres` for a Drizzle-native Postgres store with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` claims, `redis` for an atomic-Lua Redis backend, and `testing` for conformance drivers. Every attempt is persisted in a run ledger, dedup, throttle, debounce, and cross-process cancellation work with Effect fibers, and metrics integrate with the Effect `Metric` system. Drizzle-kit owns migrations because the job tables are plain schema factories users re-export.

Teams already running Effect services that need durable, observable background work — email sends, image processing, scheduled data pipelines — get compile-time wiring of stores to jobs, runtime safety from `Schema.Redacted`, and the same control primitives (`timeout`, `interrupt`, `pause`) they use elsewhere in their app.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> FireMigrate migrates data from Firebase Firestore (collections and nested subcollections), Firebase Authentication users, and Firebase Storage object metadata into PostgreSQL, making it a practical bridge for teams moving from Firebase to Supabase or any Postgres-based backend. It is safe by default: every operation runs as a dry run unless `--write` is passed alongside `dryRun: false`, and re-running is idempotent because rows are upserted by document id. Schema inference samples documents and routes unexpected fields into a `_extra` JSON column so later additions are not lost, while subcollections are discovered by walking parent documents up to 20 levels deep and flattened into namespaced tables like `users__posts__comments`. The CLI also exposes an agent-friendly `tables` command that emits a JSON manifest of destination tables for downstream automation, and an optional hash-mode rebuild of Firebase password hashes into `$fbscrypt$` form for later Supabase Auth import. The tool is written in TypeScript/Node.js (run via `npx` or `pnpm`), targets PostgreSQL 14+ through `DATABASE_URL`, and is aimed at developers and platform engineers performing one-time Firebase-to-Postgres cutovers.

> KADATH is an open-source framework that applies Darwinian evolution to AI agent development, automatically generating and progressively improving agents optimized for a user-specified goal. Rather than relying on a single prompt or agent design, it spawns a population of agents that compete across multiple generations, are independently graded against a measurable benchmark, learn from top performers, mutate, and reproduce—producing increasingly capable solutions through repeated selection. The architecture is split into two strictly separated layers: a non-evolving kernel that controls scheduling, benchmarking, grading, lineage, isolation, and resource management, and the organisms (evolvable agents) whose full framework—including system prompt, Python code, tools, and dependencies—forms the genome subject to mutation between epochs. Agents can inspect but not modify their own code during a run, preventing them from manipulating their fitness scores. Key features include a model-driven Architect that converts natural-language goals into validated, contract-conforming benchmarks with locked hashes; an interactive CLI for configuring goals, epoch duration, population size, and iteration counts; full Git-based genome lineage with duplicate-rejection; read-only container isolation per organism; rich telemetry combining high-level activity logs with detailed execution traces; and automatic first-boot provisioning of PostgreSQL, MinIO, LiteLLM, and SearXNG services via Docker.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Lead is a Postgres text-search extension that provides a deliberately non-production implementation of TIN-compatible application SQL for use in development, test, CI, and staging environments. It implements the `tin` access method, the `==>` operator, full TINQL parsing and tokenization, and scoring functions (`tin.score`, `tin.full_score`, `tin.max_score`, `tin.highlight`), prioritizing correctness and a small code footprint over query performance. Every index scan returns all heap pages as candidates and relies on Postgres for visibility checks and exact TINQL/MVCC reevaluation, meaning the index stores no search data and requires no shared memory, preload libraries, or post-crash rebuilding. Target users are developers and teams needing to exercise TIN-style queries against realistic application SQL at small scale, particularly PlanetScale customers validating behavior before deploying to production TIN. The extension is built with Rust using `cargo-pgrx` (pinned to 0.19.1), targets Postgres 17 and 18, and ships with accompanying mdBook documentation covering the TINQL query language.

It solves the problem of monitoring database health without deploying agents, agents/daemons, or granting write privileges—useful for SREs, DBAs, and platform engineers who need safe, scriptable insight into managed databases like RDS or Aurora where OS-level installation isn't possible. Key features include a graded health score with CRITICAL/WARNING/NOTE/GOOD bucketing, delta tracking from a local baseline to surface regressions, focused drill-down commands (`indexes`, `queries`, `tables`, `vacuum`) for specific subsystems, an LLM-powered `ask`/`explain` mode for plain-language readings, and a `--json` contract for automation. The tool ships with cosign-signed releases and SHA256 checksum verification, and enforces read-only behavior via a dedicated `pg_monitor` role, `default_transaction_read_only` session settings, and per-query `BEGIN READ ONLY` wrappers. Written in Go and distributed as a single static binary, it's installable via script, `go install`, Docker, or Homebrew.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> restoredrill is a CI-native verification tool that proves PostgreSQL and MySQL backups actually restore, not just that backup jobs succeeded. It fetches the latest backup, restores it into a throwaway container, runs tiered checks (file freshness/RPO, structural integrity, row counts and custom SQL assertions, RTO timing, and environment sanity), and emits a JSON report with timestamped, auditor-friendly fields rather than relying on logs or self-attested policy documents. Every check fails closed, invalid configurations are rejected at load time, and notification delivery failures surface as findings so an audit cannot quietly skip a broken run. An `existing_connection` mode skips restore tiers for environments that already maintain a fresh copy, running the same read-path checks instead. The tool targets engineering and compliance teams pursuing SOC 2, ISO 27001, or AWS Foundational Technical Review who need reproducible evidence with stable schema fields in `"YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC"` format that survive copying into spreadsheets. Built in Go with a YAML configuration, it operates as a scheduled CLI job rather than a continuously running daemon, fitting cleanly into existing backup pipelines without production credentials.

The platform is built with React and Ant Design on the frontend, TypeScript with Express.js on the backend, and PostgreSQL for data storage, with Redis caching, S3-compatible storage via SeaweedFS or cloud providers, and Nginx as a reverse proxy. Docker Compose orchestration enables quick local or production-ready deployments with SSL/TLS, automated backups, and a management script for common operations.

**Product Description Text**:
> CLI that finds YC founders' emails and sends a personal note from your Gmail, built for the author's job search. GH: 1★, pushed 2026-10-08.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> A command-line tool that automates outreach to Y Combinator founders for engineers seeking startup roles, scraping YC's public directory for companies and founders, then discovering contact emails through website scraping, GitHub commit metadata, and SMTP-verified pattern guessing. It sends personalized templated emails through a user's own Gmail account with built-in throttling, daily caps, and randomized delays to stay under spam radar, while a Postgres backend tracks each contact through queued, sent, replied, and bounced states. Users can queue only high-confidence contacts, preview messages, run A/B tests across multiple subject lines, and automatically detect replies and bounces by scanning their Gmail inbox. The tool requires Python 3.10+, PostgreSQL, outbound port 25 access for SMTP verification, and a Gmail account with 2-Step Verification enabled for App Password authentication. It's best suited for job-seeking engineers comfortable with the command line who want to run targeted, data-driven cold outreach campaigns at YC-backed startups.

**Product Description Text**:
> The open source Firebase alternative. Supabase gives you a dedicated Postgres database to build your web, mobile, and AI applications.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Supabase is an open-source Postgres development platform that provides a Firebase-like developer experience for building web, mobile, and AI applications. It combines enterprise-grade tools—including a hosted PostgreSQL database, PostgREST for auto-generated REST and GraphQL APIs, GoTrue for JWT-based authentication, realtime websocket subscriptions, S3-compatible file storage, edge functions, and a vector/embeddings toolkit for AI workloads. Developers can use it as a managed cloud service or self-host it locally, with modular client libraries available for JavaScript, Flutter, Swift, and other languages. The platform is aimed at developers seeking a scalable, relational backend without vendor lock-in, leveraging Postgres as its foundation. Community support is provided through GitHub Discussions, Discord, and dedicated issue tracking, while an intuitive dashboard simplifies database management and configuration.

**Product Description Text**:
> real time face swap and one-click video deepfake with only a single image (uncensored)

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Deep-Live-Cam enables real-time face swapping and one-click video deepfake creation using just a single source image, eliminating the need for extensive training data or complex model preparation. The tool supports live webcam feeds as well as pre-recorded video processing, making it accessible for streaming, content creation, and entertainment purposes such as creating personalized movie experiences, memes, or live performances. Key features include a Mouth Mask function to preserve natural lip movement, multi-face mapping for swapping different faces onto multiple subjects simultaneously, and built-in content moderation checks that block nudity, graphic material, and sensitive footage before processing. The project provides optimized pre-built binaries for Windows, macOS (Apple Silicon), and CPU-only environments, with optional GPU acceleration through CUDA for Nvidia hardware. It targets content creators, streamers, meme artists, and developers in the AI-generated media industry while requiring GPU support (NVIDIA/AMD/Apple Silicon) for optimal real-time performance. The tech stack leverages ONNX-based face-swapping models (inswapper_128_fp16), GFPGANv1.4 for face enhancement, PyTorch, and ONNX Runtime execution providers, with Python 3.14 as the recommended runtime.

Each DESIGN.md captures analyzed design tokens, typography, color palettes, spacing rules, and component patterns from brands like Vercel, Linear, Supabase, Notion, Cursor, and dozens more. Developers drop the file into their project root and instruct an AI coding agent to generate UI that visually matches the chosen brand's design language — no Figma exports or JSON schemas required. The concept builds on Google's Stitch DESIGN.md format, leveraging markdown as a format that LLMs parse natively for consistent, high-quality output. The repository is community-driven, regularly updated, and includes a request system for analyzing additional sites on demand. It targets developers, designers, and "vibecoders" who want production-ready aesthetic consistency when shipping AI-generated interfaces.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Context7 solves the problem of LLMs and AI code editors generating outdated, hallucinated, or version-mismatched code by injecting up-to-date, version-specific documentation and code examples directly into prompts. Users can invoke it by adding phrases like "use context7" to their prompts or specifying a library ID (e.g., `/supabase/supabase`) to fetch targeted docs, and it supports specifying exact versions such as "Next.js 14" for accurate results. It works in two modes: a CLI + Skills workflow (`npx ctx7 setup` with OAuth authentication and automatic API key generation) and a native MCP server integration (`https://mcp.context7.com/mcp`) compatible with Cursor, Claude Code, OpenCode, and 30+ other clients. Key tools include `resolve-library-id` and `query-docs` for library matching and documentation retrieval, alongside a TypeScript SDK and Vercel AI SDK integration. The platform is built with Node.js (requiring version 18+) and distributed as multiple packages including `@upstash/context7-mcp`, the `ctx7` CLI, `@upstash/context7-sdk`, and `@upstash/context7-tools-ai-sdk`. It is aimed at developers using AI coding assistants who need reliable, current API references without leaving their editor.

It solves the friction between visual design tools and code by mapping DOM elements back to their source code, allowing users to drag, drop, and rearrange components visually while simultaneously viewing and editing the underlying code in real-time. Key features include AI-assisted project creation from text or images, a browser-based DOM editor with live preview, branching for design experiments, checkpoint saves, one-click deployment with custom domains, and a real-time code editor with CLI access. Its architecture leverages CodeSandboxSDK for sandboxed execution, Supabase and Drizzle for data persistence, OpenRouter and the AI SDK for LLM integration, Freestyle for hosting, and Bun for the monorepo runtime, with plans to expand support beyond the Next.js and Tailwind ecosystem.

> Sockudo is a high-performance, self-hosted realtime server written in Rust that provides a drop-in replacement for Pusher, supporting both Pusher-compatible WebSocket/HTTP APIs (Protocol V1) and a native protocol (Protocol V2) with advanced delivery semantics. It solves the problem of needing scalable, low-latency pub/sub messaging with features beyond Pusher's offering, including message recovery, rewind, durable history, mutable messages, presence tracking, annotations, and tag filtering. The server supports horizontal fanout via Redis, NATS, Kafka, RabbitMQ, Pulsar, and other adapters, plus a push notification pipeline for FCM, APNs, Web Push, HMS, and WNS. It includes first-party client SDKs for JavaScript, Swift, Kotlin, Flutter, .NET, and Python, along with server-side SDKs for backend publishing, and an optional AI Transport built on the same primitives for streaming AI workloads. Sockudo is intended for developers and teams requiring realtime features—chat, notifications, live updates, collaborative apps, or AI streaming—who want Pusher compatibility without vendor lock-in, or who need richer semantics like message versioning, idempotent publishing, and two-tier recovery. Deployment is flexible, with Docker Compose, Helm charts, Prometheus metrics, webhooks, rate limiting, and TLS support for production use.

**Product Description Text**:
> Syncular is an offline-first data synchronization framework that keeps an SQLite database on each client and reconciles changes through a server-owned commit log, enabling apps to read locally and continue working without connectivity. Writes update local state immediately, enter an outbox, and are validated by the server during sync, with a formally specified wire protocol verified by shared byte-level conformance tests across both TypeScript and Rust cores. The browser client uses SQLite on OPFS, while native platforms—Rust, Swift, Kotlin, Flutter, React Native, and Tauri—share the Rust core and native SQLite bindings. Servers run on Bun, Node, or Cloudflare Workers and support SQLite, Postgres, or D1 storage backends. Optional packages provide Yjs CRDT integration, column-level encryption, schema/query code generation for multiple languages, React hooks, and an in-process testkit for deterministic fault-injection testing. It targets developers building offline-capable, multi-platform applications who need reliable local-first storage with conflict-free replication without giving up SQL.

**Product Description Text**:
> KalamDB is a lightweight, real-time, storage-efficient SQL database designed as a unified backend for AI agents and frontend applications. It solves the problem of maintaining separate CRUD APIs, sync layers, and agent tools by exposing a single SQL interface over HTTP, with live row subscriptions over WebSocket, eliminating the need for custom REST or GraphQL layers per workflow. The platform features per-user data isolation through USER tables and an `EXECUTE AS USER` mechanism, ensuring access remains policy-scoped rather than broadly exposed, while supporting built-in auth via Basic, JWT, and OAuth 2.0 providers. Its hybrid storage engine combines RocksDB for active writes with Parquet for compressed historical data, and it extends functionality with vector embeddings for AI workloads, pub/sub topics, consumer groups, and Multi-Raft distributed clustering. Built in Rust with official TypeScript, Dart/Flutter, and Rust client SDKs, KalamDB targets agent-native app developers, product teams building chat UIs and approval flows, and operators needing an integrated data plane with Admin UI, CLI tooling, and portable object storage across S3, GCS, and Azure.

**Product Description Text**:
> Firemigrate: open-source CLI moving Firebase data to PostgreSQL ('Inspect first. Write last.'), `npx @ezekielreu6/firemigrate`; read-only inspection, schema preview, dry runs by default. GH: 2★.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> FireMigrate migrates data from Firebase Firestore (collections and nested subcollections), Firebase Authentication users, and Firebase Storage object metadata into PostgreSQL, making it a practical bridge for teams moving from Firebase to Supabase or any Postgres-based backend. It is safe by default: every operation runs as a dry run unless `--write` is passed alongside `dryRun: false`, and re-running is idempotent because rows are upserted by document id. Schema inference samples documents and routes unexpected fields into a `_extra` JSON column so later additions are not lost, while subcollections are discovered by walking parent documents up to 20 levels deep and flattened into namespaced tables like `users__posts__comments`. The CLI also exposes an agent-friendly `tables` command that emits a JSON manifest of destination tables for downstream automation, and an optional hash-mode rebuild of Firebase password hashes into `$fbscrypt$` form for later Supabase Auth import. The tool is written in TypeScript/Node.js (run via `npx` or `pnpm`), targets PostgreSQL 14+ through `DATABASE_URL`, and is aimed at developers and platform engineers performing one-time Firebase-to-Postgres cutovers.

> FlashAttention is a fast, memory-efficient implementation of exact attention that uses an IO-aware tiling strategy to minimize memory reads/writes between GPU HBM and SRAM, dramatically reducing the memory and computational cost of transformer attention. It provides official implementations of FlashAttention, FlashAttention-2, a beta FlashAttention-3 optimized for NVIDIA Hopper GPUs (with FP16/BF16 and FP8 forward support), and FlashAttention-4 written in CuTeDSL for Hopper and Blackwell architectures. The library supports NVIDIA CUDA (Ampere, Ada, Hopper GPUs) as well as AMD ROCm via both Composable Kernel and Triton backends, with features including causal masking, variable sequence lengths, MQA/GQA, dropout, rotary embeddings, ALiBi, and paged attention. It targets deep learning researchers and engineers training or deploying large transformer models who need significant speedups and memory savings. The stack is built primarily in CUDA and Python, requiring PyTorch 2.2+, with support for fp16 and bf16 datatypes and head dimensions up to 256.

> **second-brain** is a personal knowledge engine that turns UI inspiration captured from anywhere into a private, agent-ready design wiki. Users share posts, pages, screenshots or videos from their phone or Mac via a Shortcut; a vision model reads each capture, measures its pixel palette, extracts patterns, and files it under a topic (design, features, tools, practices) in a Markdown wiki kept in a separate private repository. Recurring choices across captures are distilled into a taste profile and a `DESIGN.md` with contrast-checked design tokens, which Claude reads through the `second-brain` skill before building UI, making the agent's output match the user's established aesthetic. A weekly lint pass merges duplicate topics, splits catch-alls and rewrites affected pages, ensuring the navigation stays clean. The stack is deliberately minimal: Supabase as an inbox, GitHub Actions and Ollama Cloud (or a local Ollama) for analysis, `ntfy` for push notifications, and plain Markdown with frontmatter as the storage format, with no database or frontend to maintain. It's aimed at designers, indie hackers and developers who want their coding agent to build interfaces that consistently reflect their taste without manually curating references each time.

**Product Description Text**:
> Bramble is a local-first, end-to-end encrypted password manager that keeps user vaults stored on personal devices rather than on company servers, eliminating the risk of third-party breaches. It solves the trust problem inherent to cloud-based password managers by syncing vaults directly between a user's own devices via a private peer-to-peer mesh, with no relay server holding plaintext data. The platform supports Chromium browsers and Firefox via an extension, plus native iOS and Android apps featuring system AutoFill, biometric unlock (Face ID, Touch ID, Android biometrics), and passkey support. All cryptographic operations run in a shared Rust core compiled to WebAssembly on desktop and as a native library on mobile, using Argon2id key derivation, AES-256-GCM encryption, and per-entry envelope encryption, with secrets wiped from memory after use. Beyond syncing, Bramble offers multiple backup strategies, including encrypted `.bramble` file exports, KeePass `.kdbx` exports, and scheduled ciphertext-only backups to Dropbox, S3-compatible storage, or self-hosted WebDAV. It is aimed at privacy-conscious users and self-hosters who want full control over their credentials without vendor lock-in.

- **Catalog Provenance**: Channel: *Github Awesome* | Video: *GitHub Trending Weekly #41: canvas-ui, openworker, thinking-orbs, no-ai-slop, sticker-forge, justif* | Published: *2026-07-25*
- **Attached Keywords**: `sqlite, database, tools, rust`

**Product Description Text**:
> minisqlite is a from-scratch reimplementation of SQLite written in Rust, providing a full SQL database engine with parser, query planner and executor, transactions, and a storage engine that reads and writes SQLite's official on-disk file format. It exposes a deliberately minimal public API consisting of a single `Connection` type with four methods (`open`, `open_in_memory`, `execute`, `query`), plus the `Value`, `Row`, and `Error` types, making it suitable for embedding in Rust applications that need SQLite-compatible persistence without linking against the C library. The implementation spans roughly 200,000 lines across 14 layered crates covering the SQL dialect (including joins, CTEs, window functions, upserts, generated columns, triggers, and foreign keys), about 90 built-in functions, ~20 PRAGMAs, WAL and rollback-journal modes, and ~5,650 tests. It uses only one external dependency (`elsa`, for the page cache) and contains no `unsafe` code in library code, making it attractive for projects that prioritize memory safety and a small dependency surface. The intended audience includes systems programmers, database researchers, and developers who need a verifiable, auditable, format-compatible SQL engine in pure Rust.

It surfaces a health score along with key signals—connection usage, cache hit ratio, blocked locks, slow-query regressions, unused indexes, vacuum age, and replication lag—and exposes five detail views (inspect, queries, indexes, tables, "why") plus a command bar for ad-hoc questions. Built in Rust and shipped as a single binary, it leans on pgbot for read-only diagnostics, so it never writes to the database, opens a SQL console, or runs shell commands. Configuration stores only environment-variable names rather than connection strings, and credentials are scrubbed from logs, screen output, and child-process argv, making it safe to use on shared hosts and in CI. Installation is a one-line curl that pulls a checksum-verified release and pgbot itself; a built-in demo with three fake databases lets new users explore every view without provisioning a real cluster.

**Product Description Text**:
> *(No brief description text provided in original record)*

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> redis-lua-py lets developers write Redis Lua scripts as native Python functions instead of opaque strings, addressing the common pain points of editor highlighting, linting, and type checking being unavailable in traditional string-based Lua definitions. At import time, the library parses a restricted Python subset, compiles it into Lua, checks Redis command names against the official command table, and dispatches the result with `EVALSHA` (or `FCALL` for Redis Functions), producing a stable hash that makes the server's script cache cold only once per script. Scripts support typed parameters where annotated `Key` arguments become `KEYS` for Cluster routing, `int`/`float` values are wrapped in `tonumber`, module-level constants are folded in as literals, and `bytes` values pass through unchanged without decoding. It works with both sync and async clients from redis-py 4.2+ and coredis, and exposes the generated Lua on each script for code review and golden-file testing. A `python -m redis_lua_py generate` command emits a standalone module of typed functions with no runtime dependency on the package, and a `--check` flag keeps generated code in sync during CI.

The service offers features such as web search, comprehensive scraping, and advanced interaction capabilities like clicking and scrolling. Firecrawl ensures LLM-ready output, delivering data in formats like markdown, JSON, and screenshots, which significantly reduces token usage for AI applications. Built for speed and reliability, it acts as a crucial data layer, enabling AI agents to gather and process real-time web information efficiently.

> IPTV, open database of IPTV channels. IPTV is an open source repository that maintains a large collection of publicly available IPTV channel playlists

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> A community-maintained repository aggregating publicly available IPTV channels from around the world into curated M3U playlists that can be loaded directly into any compatible video player like VLC. Users can access a master playlist containing all channels or browse categorized playlists via the PLAYLISTS.md file, while an Electronic Program Guide (EPG) is available through a companion repository. Channel metadata is sourced from a separate structured database, and developers can interact with the data via a dedicated REST API. The project serves cord-cutters, IPTV app developers, and researchers needing an organized catalog of free, publicly broadcast stream URLs. No video files are hosted; the repository only collects and links to stream sources that copyright holders have intentionally published openly. Licensed under CC0, it includes built-in processes for handling copyright claims and welcomes community contributions for adding or correcting channels.

> RAGFlow is an open-source Retrieval-Augmented Generation engine that combines advanced RAG capabilities with Agent functionality to deliver high-quality context for large language models. It addresses the challenge of extracting reliable, grounded answers from complex unstructured data by providing deep document understanding, template-based chunking, and traceable citations that reduce hallucinations. The platform supports a wide range of data sources including Word, Excel, PDF, images, scanned documents, and web pages, while offering configurable LLM and embedding model integration with fused re-ranking for improved retrieval accuracy. Developers and enterprises can leverage its streamlined RAG orchestration, agentic workflows, MCP support, and pre-built agent templates to build production-ready AI systems with minimal complexity. Deployment is flexible, with options including a hosted cloud service, Docker images, and self-hosting via source code. The stack is Python-based (3.13+) and designed to scale from individual projects to large enterprise deployments.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> GraphRAG is a data pipeline and transformation suite developed by Microsoft Research that extracts meaningful, structured data from unstructured text using LLMs and knowledge graph memory structures to enhance question-answering capabilities. It addresses the limitations of traditional Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems by constructing graph-based representations of private datasets, enabling LLMs to reason more effectively over narrative or domain-specific information. Key features include a modular indexing pipeline, prompt tuning guidance for optimizing outputs on custom data, and support for migration between versions to preserve prior indexing work. It is intended for researchers and developers working with private or narrative text corpora who need targeted context retrieval, though users should note that indexing can be computationally expensive. The project is implemented in Python (distributed via PyPI) and is currently maintained in a largely maintenance mode, with bug fixes and dependency updates but no new feature development.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Delta Lake is an open-source storage framework that brings ACID transactions and a Lakehouse architecture to data lakes, bridging the gap between traditional data warehouses and flexible cloud storage. It provides reliable, scalable table storage with full transactional support, enabling concurrent reads and writes, schema enforcement, and time travel on data stored in formats like Parquet. The framework integrates seamlessly with major compute engines including Apache Spark, PrestoDB, Trino, Apache Flink, and Apache Hive, and offers APIs for Scala, Java, Rust, Ruby, and Python. Underlying storage systems must provide atomic visibility, mutual exclusion, and consistent listing to maintain Delta Lake's ACID guarantees. Backward compatibility is guaranteed across versions, while forward compatibility may be broken as the transaction protocol evolves with new features. Data engineers and platform teams building large-scale analytics, ETL, and streaming pipelines use Delta Lake to unify batch and streaming workloads on a single, reliable storage layer.

**Product Description Text**:
> High-performance retrieval engine for unstructured data

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> dsRAG is a high-performance retrieval engine designed for unstructured data, particularly excelling at complex queries over dense, lengthy documents like financial reports, legal filings, and academic papers. It addresses the limitations of vanilla RAG systems—which struggle with questions requiring synthesis across multiple text sections—by introducing three core techniques: semantic sectioning, AutoContext, and Relevant Segment Extraction (RSE). Semantic sectioning uses an LLM to partition documents into coherent segments with descriptive titles, while AutoContext prepends document- and section-level metadata to chunks before embedding, dramatically improving retrieval precision. Relevant Segment Extraction clusters related chunks at query time and intelligently reassembles them into longer, contextually complete segments tailored to the question. The library supports multiple vector databases including Faiss, Chroma, Weaviate, Qdrant, Milvus, and Pinecone, and is installable via pip with optional dependency groups. Benchmarks demonstrate substantial accuracy gains, achieving 96.6% on FinanceBench compared to 32% for vanilla RAG, and an average score improvement from 4.72 to 8.42 on the KITE benchmark. It is well-suited for AI engineers and developers building production-grade RAG applications where retrieval quality over complex document corpora is critical.

The tool solves the problem of the official standard being available only in dense LaTeX format by transforming it into clean, linkable Markdown while preserving stable cross-file references between chapters.

The converter uses a three-stage pipeline built on Pandoc 3.x with Lua 5.4 filters for the heavy lifting, wrapped by Python for repository management and output formatting. Custom Lua filters handle C++ standard-specific constructs including code blocks (`\begin{codeblock}`), grammar notation (BNF variants), section headings (`\rSec0` through `\rSec3`), and 50+ custom macros like `\tcode{}` and `\Cpp`. Users can convert any standard version via git tags, branches, or SHAs, with pre-converted versions already available for C++11 (n3337) through C++26 (trunk). The tool supports multiple modes including single-file output, separate chapter files with automatic cross-link fixing, and version diff generation for HTML site builds. It targets C++ developers, committee members, language lawyers, and educators who need accessible, searchable versions of the standard, and is released into the public domain under the Unlicense.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Crossfoot reads invoice PDFs by separating the problem of locating data from the problem of transcribing it: a language model points at where values sit on the page, ordinary code copies the values from the PDF text, and the document's printed totals are used to prove the read. A successful read produces a small JSON "reading spec" describing the layout, so subsequent invoices of the same shape are processed in milliseconds with no model call and no network access. Accountants, finance teams, AP automation developers, and anyone who needs to convert varied PDF invoices into trustworthy structured data benefit most, since the tool detects tampering or OCR mistakes via built-in cross-foot checks and returns unproven reads with the failed check rather than silently producing wrong totals. Built on Node.js 20+ as an ES module package, it exposes a CLI (`crossfoot invoice.pdf`) and a programmatic API (`createReader`), with pluggable model adapters (Anthropic supported) and pluggable spec stores. Output preserves the document's original text formatting for numbers and dates, names columns after the headings printed on the page, and returns a typed result with `proven`, `rows`, `via`, and `problem` fields so callers can decide how to handle unproven documents.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Zep is a managed agent memory platform, and this repository serves as a central hub for example code, framework integrations, and tooling that help developers build AI agents with persistent, long-term memory. It addresses the challenge of giving LLM-based agents the ability to retain context, recall facts across sessions, and ingest structured or unstructured data such as Slack messages, documents, and emails. The repository provides SDK examples in Python, TypeScript, and Go, alongside integration packages for popular agent frameworks including LangGraph, CrewAI, Microsoft AutoGen, AG2, Pydantic AI, LiveKit, Strands Agents, Mastra, and Vercel AI SDK. It also includes `zep-ingest` for bulk data ingestion, a default ontology for memory structuring, memory benchmarks (LoCoMo, LongMemEval), and an evaluation harness for testing retrieval quality. The target users are AI engineers and developers building production-grade agentic applications who need reliable, scalable memory infrastructure beyond simple conversation buffers.

**Product Description Text**:
> The open source Firebase alternative. Supabase gives you a dedicated Postgres database to build your web, mobile, and AI applications.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Supabase is an open-source Postgres development platform that provides a Firebase-like developer experience for building web, mobile, and AI applications. It combines enterprise-grade tools—including a hosted PostgreSQL database, PostgREST for auto-generated REST and GraphQL APIs, GoTrue for JWT-based authentication, realtime websocket subscriptions, S3-compatible file storage, edge functions, and a vector/embeddings toolkit for AI workloads. Developers can use it as a managed cloud service or self-host it locally, with modular client libraries available for JavaScript, Flutter, Swift, and other languages. The platform is aimed at developers seeking a scalable, relational backend without vendor lock-in, leveraging Postgres as its foundation. Community support is provided through GitHub Discussions, Discord, and dedicated issue tracking, while an intuitive dashboard simplifies database management and configuration.


#### 2. [remix](https://github.com/remix-run/remix) (`remix-run/remix`)

- **Attached Keywords**: `inference, nextjs, web, framework, typescript`

**Product Description Text**:
> Build Better Websites. Create modern, resilient user experiences with web fundamentals.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Remix is a web framework designed for building modern, resilient user experiences grounded in web fundamentals. It tackles the complexity of full-stack web development by emphasizing Model-First Development, web standards, runtime-first design, minimal dependencies, and composable abstractions—all distributed under a single `remix` package for simplicity. The framework leverages server-side web APIs like Web Streams, Web Crypto, Blob, and File, ensuring code is portable by default across Node.js, Bun, Deno, and Cloudflare Workers. Developers benefit from a rich ecosystem of standalone packages covering routing, authentication, sessions, data validation, file storage, SQL query building, and HTTP middleware, each usable independently or composed together. This makes Remix well-suited for web developers seeking a future-proof, runtime-agnostic toolkit that prioritizes interoperability and AI-friendly abstractions.


#### 3. [surrealdb](https://github.com/surrealdb/surrealdb) (`surrealdb/surrealdb`)
- **Official URL**: [https://github.com/surrealdb/surrealdb](https://github.com/surrealdb/surrealdb)

- **Attached Keywords**: `devops, rust, database, mcp, llm`
- **GitHub Topics**: `backend-as-a-service, cloud-database, database, database-as-a-service, developer-tools, devtools, distributed, distributed-database, document-database, graph-database, iot-database, nosql, realtime-database, serverless`

**Product Description Text**:
> A scalable, distributed, collaborative, document-graph database, for the realtime web

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> SurrealDB is a scalable, distributed, multi-model database written in Rust that unifies document, graph, relational, time-series, geospatial, and key-value data types into a single engine. It eliminates the need for most server-side components by combining database and API backend functionality, including real-time live queries, WebSocket connections, end-user authentication, and granular row-level permissions. The database supports SQL-like querying through SurrealQL, as well as GraphQL, ACID transactions, full-text and vector indexing, and graph traversal without JOINs. It can be deployed as a single Rust binary running embedded in applications, in the browser via WebAssembly, at the edge, self-hosted, or scaled across distributed clusters in the cloud. Developers building AI agent data layers, knowledge graphs, recommendation engines, fraud detection systems, and other data-intensive applications use SurrealDB to simplify infrastructure and accelerate development. The project offers official client libraries for JavaScript, Python, .NET, PHP, and more, plus an MCP server for LLM integration.

> A next.js web application that integrates AI capabilities with draw.io diagrams. This app allows you to create, modify, and enhance diagrams through natural language commands and AI-assisted visualization.

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Next AI Draw.io is a Next.js web application that brings AI-powered diagram creation to draw.io, allowing users to generate, modify, and enhance diagrams through natural language prompts instead of manual drawing. It supports image-based diagram replication, PDF and text file ingestion, and offers diagram history with version control so users can preview and restore previous iterations. The app is accessible via a hosted demo, a cross-platform desktop application, Docker, or one-click deployment to Vercel, Tencent EdgeOne Pages, and Cloudflare Workers. An MCP server integration enables AI agents like Claude Desktop, Cursor, and VS Code to generate diagrams in real time, while multi-provider LLM support (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, ByteDance Doubao, and others) gives users flexibility to bring their own API keys. Developers, architects, technical writers, and educators who need to quickly produce flowcharts, cloud architectures, or conceptual diagrams will find it especially useful, with the entire stack built on Next.js and React.

- **Attached Keywords**: `framework, typescript, tools, inference`

**Product Description Text**:
> scriptc is a TypeScript-to-native compiler that produces small, self-contained executables from ordinary TypeScript code without requiring Node, V8, or any embedded JavaScript engine by default. It addresses the long-standing gap between TypeScript's developer ergonomics and the deployment cost of shipping a full Node runtime, using a three-tier execution model: code is either compiled statically to native, runs through an embedded QuickJS engine when `--dynamic` is opted into for `any`-typed code and npm dependencies, or fails the build with a specific diagnostic—nothing is silently miscompiled. The compiler leverages TypeScript's own type checker and frontend via the tsc API, lowers to a typed IR, and emits either LLVM or C (via clang), with a vendored C runtime that provides refcounted values, a cycle collector, stackful fibers for async/await, a dependency-free event loop (kqueue), and the server stack (net, http, https, tls with mbedTLS, dns, fetch with WHATWG streams). Key features include differential testing against Node on an 800+ program corpus with byte-exact output comparison, AddressSanitizer + reference-count auditing on every change, escape hatches like `comptime()` for build-time evaluation and a Native FFI for C ABI calls, and binary sizes of 170–200KB statically with ~2.4ms startup. It's aimed at TypeScript developers building CLIs, servers, proxies, and edge functions who want Node's behavior with native performance, minimal footprint, and end-to-end safety

Cloud API failures surface as tagged Effect errors, the same code runs locally, in plan/deploy, in smoke tests, and in CI, and bindings replace the usual glue code. Supported providers include AWS (S3, SQS, DynamoDB, Kinesis, Lambda, EC2) and Cloudflare (Workers, R2, D1, Durable Objects, Containers). The stack is fully self-hostable via Docker Compose using ClickHouse for high-volume span storage, Postgres for relational data, and Redis for rate limiting, with a hosted SaaS option also available. It targets developers building production AI agents and multi-step workflows who need cost attribution, alerting on thresholds, and per-customer analytics without bolting on a separate telemetry pipeline.

Each "cell" (Durable Object) is backed by its own SQLite database that gets continuously replicated to an S3-compatible bucket you control, with ownership tracked via object-storage compare-and-swap rather than a traditional consensus protocol. Nodes embed V8, execute Wrangler bundles, and coordinate entirely through the shared bucket, allowing applications to shard by construction while idle cells hibernate to near-zero resource usage. It targets developers who want the Durable Objects programming model without vendor lock-in, particularly teams building stateful edge or distributed applications on their own hardware. The stack is Rust-based with an embedded V8 runtime, integrates with standard AWS credentials, supports Wrangler-style deployments via esbuild, and includes operational tooling like `celld diagnose` plus pressure-based cell shedding.

> Cloudflare Computer is a virtual filesystem and pluggable execution environment built on Cloudflare's Durable Objects, providing a single workspace abstraction backed by authoritative SQLite state. The workspace exposes one execution entry point (`workspace.runtime.exec`) that can route to multiple interchangeable backends: a Container backend with full Linux userland via a FUSE mount and `computerd` daemon, a just-bash shell running in a Dynamic Worker, or an ECMAScript module evaluator with durable imports and `node:fs/promises` support. This lets developers choose between heavyweight sandbox execution and lightweight isolated runtimes against the same persistent filesystem, with backends connecting lazily and registering under stable IDs. The monorepo ships `@cloudflare/dofs` for the SQLite-backed VFS and sync protocol, `@cloudflare/computer-rpc` for capnweb wire types, the `computerd` daemon, and the top-level `@cloudflare/computer` package, alongside runnable examples including a chat agent, an artifacts publisher, and a tutorial that renders markdown to PDF. Performance benchmarks show the FUSE mount outperforms real disk on metadata-heavy workloads while trailing on large sequential I/O. The package is marked PREVIEW with unstable APIs, targeted at developers prototyping stateful agents, file-processing tools, and sandboxed code execution on Cloudflare's edge.

It solves the overhead and complexity of traditional container tools by starting kernel-enforced, rootless OCI containers in roughly 3.5 milliseconds with zero RAM at rest, making it practical for ephemeral, per-request workloads like AI-generated code execution, CI steps, and serverless functions. Key features include full OCI image support (pull, build, commit, push), a deny-by-default seccomp allowlist, cgroup v2 limits, and a `--security-profile untrusted` flag that bundles hardening for untrusted code; resource profiles for CPU, memory, disk, and devices declared once in `kern.toml` and reusable across both sandboxed boxes and host processes; compatibility with existing `docker-compose.yml` files via `kern compose`; and a Python/Node binding plus an MCP server for integrating with LangChain, Claude Desktop, or Cursor. Its dependency tree is intentionally minimal—just `libc`—with JSON and OCI parsing done by hand and image pulls delegated to the host's `curl` and `tar`. Target users are developers and platform engineers who need fast, lightweight, hardened isolation for untrusted or short-lived workloads, including AI agent builders, CI/CD pipeline authors, and embedded/edge deployments on x86_64, aarch64 boards, or WSL2.

> open-compute delivers a self-hosted, Cloudflare Workers–compatible platform packaged as a single binary, eliminating the need for Kubernetes, Redis, Postgres, or distributed control planes. It bundles the workerd runtime, control plane, scheduler, and all product bindings (KV, R2, D1, Durable Objects, Queues, etc.) into one file that uses SQLite for platform metadata and the local filesystem for object storage by default, with S3-compatible storage as an optional drop-in. Built on a pinned, checksum-verified fork of workerd, it achieves millisecond cold starts and MB-scale memory by running workers in isolates rather than per-request processes or containers, and it remains fully usable offline at startup. Developers can deploy standard module workers using familiar Wrangler workflows against a local `/client/v4` API, with claimed 99% coverage of the documented Workers API surface across 2,203 tracked members and validated compatibility on real Cloudflare products. The project targets teams who want Cloudflare's developer experience on their own hardware—edge platforms, on-prem workloads, or anyone seeking to avoid vendor lock-in—written primarily in Rust with cross-platform support for macOS and Linux.

**Product Description Text**:
> ⚠️ Browser fingerprinting via favicon!

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> Supercookie demonstrates a browser fingerprinting technique that exploits the favicon cache (F-Cache) to assign persistent, unique identifiers to website visitors. By serving favicons from a combinatorial set of URL paths and observing which requests are made versus served from cache, a server can reconstruct a binary pattern that identifies a browser with 100% accuracy. Unlike conventional cookies, this tracking method survives cache flushing, browser restarts, VPN usage, incognito/private mode, and even certain anti-tracking service workers, making it a significant privacy concern. The repository includes a fully functional web server (deployable via Docker or Node.js) that performs the favicon-based tracking, along with a live demo and comprehensive documentation explaining the threat model. Inspired by academic research from the University of Illinois, Chicago, it serves as an educational tool to raise awareness of this stealth tracking vector affecting all major desktop and mobile browsers. The technology stack is lightweight, relying on a Node.js backend with a configurable environment for hosting the tracking infrastructure.

It is aimed at households, small teams, clubs, and small communities running their own reverse proxy who want closed-by-default posture without bolting an identity provider onto apps that don't support one. It automatically provisions and renews certificates from ZeroSSL and Let's Encrypt for public domains while running its own local certificate authority for internal names and IPs, with support for Encrypted ClientHello (ECH) and multi-issuer fallback. **Product Description Text**:
> *(No brief description text provided in original record)*

**Extended Synopsis / Feature Analysis**:
> OpenFlux is a network stack research tool that establishes a TCP tunnel over pluggable transports, enabling packet-level traffic forwarding through a client and exit-node architecture. It targets developers and researchers experimenting with network tunneling, transport obfuscation, and exit-node design, and ships clients for macOS (utun L3), Linux, Windows, Android, and iOS (NEPacketTunnelProvider). The exit node supports two backends selected via `--mode`: `l3`, a raw SNAT/DNAT forwarder using SOCK_RAW and conntrack on Linux with root, and `l4`, a userspace gVisor-based TCP proxy (`proxy` is a deprecated alias) that works on any platform without privileges. Transports include Yandex.Docs (WebSocket), Yandex Volga, MAX/OneMe (WebRTC DataChannel), Cups.online (Centrifugo rooms), and Mail.ru Docs, all wrapped by a batched zstd codec (`transport/batched.go`) that coalesces tunnel packets to reduce message overhead and improve throughput, with optional AES-256-GCM encryption via a shared key. The client terminates TCP locally through gVisor, utun, or NEPacketTunnelProvider and sends raw IP packets into the transport, yielding an end-to-end single TCP connection in `l3` mode and double-termination in `l4` mode. The codebase is written in Go (with platform-specific cgo for iOS) and is provided as a non-commercial, as-is research artifact.
